text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
KOHA JONE
- Thousands poured into the streets of Vlore late on Wednesday to prevent riot police from Tirana to evict students on hunger strike from their university.
- Hunger strike students are suffering from low body temperature but have refused to be treated in hospital and have decided to take serum.
- Supporters from northern town of Shkoder and the nearby towns of Berat and Fier travelled to Vlore on Wednesday to express their support.
- Berisha was cheered by civil servants and jeered by students in the southern town of Gjirokaster when he explained in handling of the pyramid scheme crisis.
- Berisha left Gjirokaster by helicopter but people blocking a road near the southern town of Memaliaj forced his escort to go by a longer route to reach Tirana.

- About 200 students at Tirana University have threatened to go on hunger strike unless President Sali Berisha meets them to discuss the pyramid scheme crisis and the fate of hunger strikers in Vlore.
- High school students in Tirana have quit classes in support of fasting students in Vlore.
- Students in Tirana have asked Higher Education Minister Besnik Gjongecaj to stop intimidation by plain-clothes policemen on their campus.
- John King, the International Monetary Fund's representative in Albania, said the IMF is considering a financial aid to the Central Bank of Albania to improve its monetary reserves.
- The National Council of the ruling Democratic Party will decide on Thursday whether to select Sali Berisha as its presidential candidate.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The European Union will send a team of experts to discuss the Albanian financial crisis and ways to help.
- The Democratic Party has invited the main opposition Socialist party to a bilateral meeting.
- The opposition Forum for Democracy has called on MPs not to elect President Berisha for a second term.
- Plain-clothes civilians have beaten Tirana high school pupils trying to reach a student campus to demonstrate in support of hunger strikers in Vlore.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- President Berisha has said European Union support is an historic appeal to Albanians and promised free trade zones from the north to the south to supporters in the southern town of Gjirokaster.
- Berisha assured Japanese businessmen Albania would carry on with reforms to develop the most liberal principles of the market economy.
- The Democratic secretary-general says the capital Tirana will never be the terrain of communists, an allusion to the opposition Socialists.
